title: Grade 2 Science — Wed, Jun 18
description: Our Food — Day 3 of 5: Types of tastes and how we sense food
subject: science

questions.question: The organ we use to taste food is the:
questions.explanation: We taste food using the tongue. Tiny bumps on the tongue called taste buds detect different tastes.

questions.question: Sugar has a ___ taste.
questions.explanation: Sugar tastes sweet. Honey, ripe fruits, and jaggery also have a sweet taste.

questions.question: Lemon juice has a ___ taste.
questions.explanation: Lemon juice tastes sour. Tamarind (imli), raw mango, and curd also have a sour taste.

questions.question: Salt has a ___ taste.
questions.explanation: Salt tastes salty. We add salt to food to make it taste better.

questions.question: Neem leaves and bitter gourd (karela) taste:
questions.explanation: Neem and karela (bitter gourd) taste bitter. Bitterness is a warning taste — many poisonous plants are bitter.

questions.question: Green chilli has a ___ taste.
questions.explanation: Green chilli is spicy (hot). The spicy taste comes from a substance called capsaicin.

questions.question: Milk has a ___ taste.
questions.explanation: Fresh milk has a mild, slightly sweet taste. When milk turns sour (curd), the taste changes.

questions.question: When we have a cold and our nose is blocked, food tastes:
questions.explanation: Smell and taste work together. When the nose is blocked, we cannot smell food, so it tastes dull.

questions.question: Which of these is a sour food?
questions.explanation: Tamarind (imli) is sour. It is used in chutneys and curries for its sour taste.

questions.question: Match: Ripe banana is ___ and raw banana is ___.
questions.explanation: Ripe bananas are sweet (sugar forms as they ripen). Raw (unripe) bananas are starchy and slightly bitter.

questions.question: Coffee and dark chocolate taste ___.
questions.explanation: Coffee and dark chocolate have a bitter taste. Sugar is usually added to make them sweeter.

questions.question: How many basic tastes does the tongue detect?
questions.explanation: Scientists say there are 5 basic tastes: sweet, sour, salty, bitter, and umami (savoury). For Grade 2 we focus on sweet, sour, salty, bitter, and spicy.

questions.question: Pickles (achar) usually taste ___ and ___.
questions.explanation: Pickles are usually sour (from vinegar or lemon) and spicy (from chillies and spices). They also have salt.

questions.question: The sense we use to smell food is located in our:
questions.explanation: We smell food using the nose. The nose helps us enjoy the aroma of food before we even taste it.

questions.question: Amla (gooseberry) is famous for tasting:
questions.explanation: Amla tastes very sour first, then leaves a slightly sweet aftertaste. It is rich in Vitamin C.
